usage: xo mod tidy [--dir=<dir>] [--json]
       xo mod graph [--dir=<dir>] [--json]
       xo mod accept-effects [--dir=<dir>] [--json] [<module path>...]
       xo mod clean
       xo mod proxy serve [--addr=127.0.0.1:7070] [--fetch] [<cache dir>]
       xo mod sumdb keygen <log name> <key file>
       xo mod sumdb serve --key=<key file> [--addr=127.0.0.1:7071] [--fetch] <data dir>

tidy requires every imported module, drops requirements nothing imports,
and rewrites xo.lock with exactly the hashes the build uses.
graph prints the requirement graph as `go mod graph` does, one
"<module>[@version] <module>@<version>" edge per line (the main module
without a version); --json adds the version selected for each module.
accept-effects records the current effects of the named modules (all
when none is named) in xo.lock (decision 0156). clean removes the module
cache. proxy serve serves a module cache read only over the module proxy
protocol (decision 0126); --fetch fills it from git on a miss.
sumdb keygen writes a new checksum log key to the file and prints the
key clients name in XO_SUMDB; sumdb serve runs a checksum log (decision
0124) with its records in <data dir>; --fetch adds a version the log
lacks from git.
